technique: The unit combines Green's parametrization of finite general linear group cuspidal characters with the attachment of ℓ-adic Galois representations to regular algebraic polarized cuspidal automorphic representations over CM fields. It uses the Galois-representation statement to obtain a uniform bound on strict localization kernels for negative Tate twists and requires a compatible chain of unitary kernels for every word in the family.

nearest.says: For a fixed number field and a fixed positive Tate twist, Soulé bounds the product of the orders of the second étale cohomology groups over primes above explicit thresholds.

nearest.says: The theorem attaches a continuous semisimple ℓ-adic Galois representation to each regular algebraic polarized cuspidal pair over a CM field, with specified Hodge–Tate weights and local–global compatibility.

nearest.says: Green matches Frobenius orbits of full size with irreducible polynomials and uses these orbits as character parameters, with a single orbit of full degree giving the cuspidal case.
nearest.quote: There are exactly as many simplexes of degree s as there are irreducible polynomials f ∈ 𝔽 of degree s.

difference: Green works over all finite fields, while the Lean parametrization uses prime fields, and the Lean Galois-representation statement uses a weaker comparison away from ℓ than the published Weil–Deligne isomorphism. VWin requires finiteness and a single bound of exp(x^ε/2) for the sum weighted by log ℓ over arbitrary finite prime sets and all positive integers e below floor(x^401), using the localization kernels for ℚℓ/ℤℓ(−e) over specified cyclotomic subfields throughout windows [Y, Y²]. The cited results provide precedents for the inputs and for cohomology bounds, while this unit combines them with the window estimate and a compatible unitary kernel chain for every word.
